analysis.title: The J.P. Morgan View: Oil Relief, CPI Stickiness, AI De-Risking: Fed Patience at Risk
key_insights: Middle East tensions de-escalated and the physical oil market moved back into surplus. Brent fell almost 20% in two weeks, from $118/bbl to about $96/bbl, close to JPM's estimated fair value.
Risk assets sold off on an abrupt AI de-risking and long-momentum unwind. DM bonds rallied at first on expectations of limited further Fed tightening at a gradual pace.
October US payrolls rose 159k, lifting the 3M average to 137k per month, the highest since May. Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%.

October CPI printed 0.35% m/m headline and 0.30% m/m core. JPM's baseline is one 25bp Fed hike in December. The tail risk is a faster cadence or larger increments, with the market pricing more than three additional hikes by September 2027.

Fed speakers lean hawkish. Waller supports a December hike and said 50bp should be considered if core CPI prints at or above 0.3% m/m. Logan signaled at least two more 25bp hikes with the option to move faster this winter. Paulson favors gradual tightening but would act more quickly if inflation expectations, wages or underlying inflation rise. Bowman is the moderating voice, preferring to wait because tighter financial conditions may already be doing some of the work.
The market now prices about 90bp of cumulative Fed hikes by September 2027, versus about 47bp one week earlier.

JPM sees the key 2027 risk as a Fed shift from a patient, growth-centric stance that tolerates above-target inflation to one committed to price stability even at the cost of growth and jobs. It calls this the 'New Testament' to 'Old Testament' shift and says it could be validated as soon as the December FOMC.
An offsetting medium-term risk is that AI diffusion caps wage acceleration, producing low unemployment with only steady wage inflation, which would complicate the Fed's reaction function.

JPM calls the equity pullback largely an AI deleveraging and positioning event that should support the durability of the AI cycle by cutting leverage and improving entry points. It reiterates its S&P 500 target of 8,000.

Long Momentum is down 38.4% from its June peak, its largest drawdown since the launch of ChatGPT. Crowding fell from the 100th to the 76th percentile. The S&P 500 forward multiple compressed by about three turns since May while index-level revisions stayed flat, which JPM reads as valuation adjustment rather than an earnings deterioration.
JPM prefers hyperscalers to high-beta AI names for balance-sheet strength and free-cash-flow durability. It also sees value in memory stocks after the recent de-rating.

Equity broadening has not crossed the threshold for a durable rotation. Of three hurdles (more Fed hikes, earnings season, midterms), the last two have eased but the first has worsened. JPM says cyclical strength is a trade, not the base case, and it is not yet ready to join the broadening camp.
Q3 earnings are running about 24% y/y growth in the US and 28% in Europe, ahead of initial estimates by 4 and 10 points. The share of S&P 500 companies raising guidance is the highest since 2021.
Democrats took both houses of Congress in the midterms. JPM treats the resulting regulation and AI-infrastructure questions as sector-specific risks rather than a market-wide event premium.

Rates: JPM took profit on 10s/30s Treasury steepeners as front-end pricing moved to very modest further easing. Its tactically bearish US rates bias was validated after CPI, but it turned neutral because the front end is now fairly priced. It neutralized its bias to overweight German versus US duration.

FX: JPM reduced but kept long USD (versus CAD, EUR, SEK), entered long NOK versus EUR and SEK, and stays long CHF and JPY as hedges and long GBP versus EUR. USD strength against low-yielding DM FX and EM FX gains have been simultaneously positive in 47% of 3-month observations in 2026, the fourth-highest frequency since 1996. The pattern has historically broken on idiosyncratic EM stress, broad financial stress or rapid Fed hiking.

Credit: JPM stays constructive on solid balance sheets, lower oil and high yields. CEMBI HY and US HY offer 8.4% yield with the best yield-to-volatility trade-off. Key risks are AI capex sustainability, European politics and a more aggressive tightening path. Year-end 2027 spread targets are 100bp (IG) and 350bp (HY) in Europe.

Hedges for an 'Old Testament' Fed: conditional bear flatteners in UST and money market curves, underweight cyclical and international stocks, broad overweight USD, underweight EM FX, HY and gold. JPM prefers the first two.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient labour market and a patient Fed support a constructive risk outlook into 2027. JPM's baseline is only one 25bp hike in December, then gradual 25bp steps with pauses. Bowman argues tighter financial conditions are already doing some tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: Strong CPI and hawkish Fed speak (Waller, Logan, Paulson) raise the risk of a faster pace or larger steps. The market prices more than three more hikes by September 2027. JPM flags a shift to an 'Old Testament' price-stability Fed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core CPI print at or above 0.3% m/m (Waller's 50bp threshold) or a December FOMC that validates the Old Testament shift would invalidate the patient-Fed case.

tension_points.bull_case: The selloff is a positioning and leverage reset. Earnings are holding, with Q3 growth around 24% y/y in the US and revisions flat. Hyperscalers offer cash generation and room to re-rate.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related pressure remains a potential source of broader financial-market stress and AI capex sustainability is a key risk. Hawkish Fed repricing could add to the drawdown.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower oil, stronger payrolls, strong earnings and the end of midterm uncertainty support a cyclical catch-up.
tension_points.bear_case: Declining inflation and a patient Fed are still missing, and the CPI print and repricing challenged broadening. JPM says broadening remains a narrow path and cyclicals are a trade, not the base case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Declining inflation and a patient Fed plus resilient growth, lower oil and de-escalation would validate broadening, per JPM's stated requirements.
